# MUD transition admission

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

given a claimed world transition, decide whether it is admissible.

## Request

A request is one line of 7 fields separated by single spaces, in this order. Anything else is answered `invalid`.

| Field | Kind | Accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | choice | `choice`, `move`, `transfer`, `engage`, `speak`, `wait` |
| `room` | number | whole number |
| `origin` | number | whole number |
| `destination` | number | whole number |
| `held` | number | whole number |
| `amount` | number | whole number |
| `capacity` | number | whole number |

The answer is one of `admissible`, `refused`, or `invalid`.

## Rules

The first rule that matches decides.

- **REQ-001** When kind is wait, the answer is `admissible`. (`rule1`)
- **REQ-002** When kind is speak, the answer is `admissible`. (`rule2`)
- **REQ-003** When kind is move and origin equals room, the answer is `admissible`. (`rule3`)
- **REQ-004** When kind is transfer and amount is at most held and amount is at most capacity, the answer is `admissible`. (`rule4`)
- **REQ-005** When kind is engage and room equals destination, the answer is `admissible`. (`rule5`)
- **Otherwise** the answer is `refused`.

## Properties

- **INV-001** It always answers `admissible` when kind is wait. not yet checked. (theorem `inv001Holds`)
- **INV-002** It always answers `admissible` when kind is speak. not yet checked. (theorem `inv002Holds`)
- **INV-003** It never answers `admissible` when kind is transfer and amount is above held. not yet checked. (theorem `inv003Holds`)
- **INV-004** It never answers `admissible` when kind is transfer and amount is above capacity. not yet checked. (theorem `inv004Holds`)
- **INV-005** It never answers `admissible` when kind is move and origin is above room. not yet checked. (theorem `inv005Holds`)
- **INV-006** It never answers `admissible` when kind is move and origin is below room. not yet checked. (theorem `inv006Holds`)
- **INV-007** It never answers `admissible` when kind is engage and room is above destination. not yet checked. (theorem `inv007Holds`)
- **INV-008** It never answers `admissible` when kind is engage and room is below destination. not yet checked. (theorem `inv008Holds`)

## Examples

- `wait 1 1 1 1 1 1` gives `admissible`
- `transfer 1 1 1 10 5 5` gives `admissible`
- `transfer 1 1 1 10 50 5` gives `refused`
- `move 5 5 9 1 1 1` gives `admissible`
- `move 5 4 9 1 1 1` gives `refused`
- `engage 3 1 3 1 1 1` gives `admissible`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
